interpretation: Each case compares graphs with and without its own AI-proposed semantic bridge under a fixed problem-family projection. Candidate question rules remain hypothetical. Neither scenario changes the official ranking.

cases.board_importance: The task reconstructs a usable hardness rule for lossless rectangle-based representation of binary images.
cases.review_state: AI-proposed semantic bridge; independent review pending

bridge.label: 3-SAT
bridge.evidence: The board source takes an explicit three-literal CNF formula and returns a satisfying assignment or NO-SOLUTION. Graph KSatisfiability<K3> uses the corresponding three-literal search variant. For exact-three clauses, use the identity map and identity witness recovery. If shorter clauses are also admitted by the board wording, use standard fresh-variable gadgets and restrict the returned assignment to the original variables. The exact clause and output conventions still require independent review.

cases.algorithmic_consequence: If the hypothetical 3-SAT to rectilinear-picture-compression rule is proved with polynomial construction and witness recovery, it provides a search-preserving hardness route for the stated picture-compression variant. The added bridge only aligns the board 3-SAT source with the graph's exact-three variant; it is not the open reduction itself.
cases.limitation: The proposed reverse bridge makes some variant pairs reachable in the baseline before the candidate is added. The candidate's marginal B and V therefore decrease; this does not mean that adding a valid graph edge destroys reachability. The bridge's exact semantic compatibility remains unreviewed.

cases.board_importance: A polynomial reduction would give both recognition and tree construction for the remaining traversal-support case.
cases.review_state: AI-proposed semantic bridge; independent review pending

bridge.label: Horn satisfiability
bridge.evidence: The board target returns a satisfying assignment or NO-SOLUTION for an explicit Horn CNF formula. Every Horn CNF formula is a CNF formula. A solution of graph Satisfiability on the identical formula is therefore a legal board output, and NO-SOLUTION is preserved. The reverse direction is invalid because arbitrary CNF is not Horn.

cases.algorithmic_consequence: If the unverified BFS-tree-support to Horn-SAT rule is correct and has polynomial construction and recovery, the source has a polynomial-time search algorithm because Horn-SAT can produce a witness or certify unsatisfiability in polynomial time.
cases.limitation: The large topology count mostly follows the Horn-SAT to general-SAT inclusion and the graph's broad SAT descendants. It must not be interpreted as 94 independent research breakthroughs.

cases.source: Common stable matching with two changed agents on each side
cases.board_importance: Moderate: a successful structured encoding would settle the first unresolved case after one-sided preference changes and could support robust market design when a few participants revise rankings. It would not classify arbitrary numbers of changed agents.
cases.review_state: AI-proposed semantic bridge; independent review pending

bridge.label: 2-SAT search
bridge.evidence: The board target returns a satisfying assignment or NO-SOLUTION for explicit 2-CNF. Graph KSatisfiability<K2> is the two-literal search variant. Convert any shorter clauses to equivalent exact-two clauses with fresh variables, then restrict a graph solution to the original variables. An empty clause is handled by a fixed unsatisfiable two-clause instance. This preserves both witness and NO-SOLUTION outputs in one call.

cases.algorithmic_consequence: If the unverified common-stable-matching to 2-SAT-search rule is correct with polynomial construction and recovery, the restricted common-stable-matching source has a polynomial-time search algorithm.
cases.limitation: Most of the 94 new problem-family relations arise because the graph contains many descendants of two-literal SAT. This reachability does not itself measure how consequential solving the restricted stable-matching question would be.
